post_outcome\.py
clauses.rationale: The publish log + self-reported outcomes are the ONLY compliant performance signal (no LinkedIn member analytics API; scraping banned by ToS). Dropping the check-in reference severs the skill's feedback loop and reverts topic/format choice to blind priors.

clauses.text: verify_sources\.py
clauses.rationale: SKILL.md must reference the source gate at all (the literal appears in the Generate research step, the Publish gate note, and Guardrails). This is a soft check that the gate isn't unreferenced; the HARD enforcement that publishing runs the gate is code-tested in tests/test_linkedin_post.py (enforce_source_gate) — not this regex.

clauses.text: (never put sources[\s\S]{0,60}?post\s+body|sources stay in the sidecar)
clauses.rationale: verify_sources never inspects the post body; keeping sources out of the body is prose-only (and in-body links also crush reach).

clauses.text: fold ~210 chars
clauses.rationale: The ~210-char '…see more' fold decides LinkedIn reach, and the fold-marked draft presentation is the only place the user actually SEES where their post cuts off before approving it. Prose-only; deleting it regresses to showing drafts with no fold visibility.

clauses.text: voice-notes\.md[^.]{0,80}same turn,?\sbefore redrafting
clauses.rationale: In-session voice corrections were lost twice in one real session (the user had to repeat the no-AI-closings rule). Persist-before-redraft lives only in this prose; deleting it regresses to corrections evaporating at session end.

clauses.text: after .{0,40}save.{0,200}before .{0,40}show
clauses.rationale: Generate flow ordering is load-bearing: research must run AFTER Save (the slug/sidecar path exists) and BEFORE Show (the shown draft is already source-backed).

clauses.text: stops? on the\s+last real point
clauses.rationale: AI-sounding endings are the user's #1, most-repeated content complaint across sessions. The pre-show ending check is prose-only; the voice_judge eval samples it but nothing else forces it at draft time.

clauses.text: never render a form\s+the user\s+didn.t\s+choose
clauses.rationale: Rendering a visual before asking wasted a full card build in a real session (user wanted a carousel). One form question before any authoring is prose-only.

clauses.text: never\s+(auto-?publish|publish[^.\n]without[^.\n]approval)
clauses.rationale: linkedin_post.py has NO approval check in code; approval-before-publish lives only in this prose. Deleting it lets the agent publish to the user's real profile without consent.

clauses.text: check-in and the menu ride in the same single
clauses.rationale: Session-start round trips are the UX tax paid every single run: the 0.14.0 pass merged the outcome check-in and the idea menu into ONE AskUserQuestion dialog. This rule is prose-only; deleting it regresses to two sequential question dialogs before any work starts.

clauses.text: (allow-unverified[^.\n]human-only|agent must never (set|self-apply) it)
clauses.rationale: --allow-unverified is the single bypass of the source gate; it is enforced only by this human-only convention.

clauses.text: transcription of a real session,\snot an\sinvention
clauses.rationale: A real session (2026-07-18) burned ~9 review rounds because the terminal card was invented instead of transcribed from the agent's actual output ('I want my terminal cards to represent my actual agents'). Capture-before-author lives only in this prose; the term-misaligned lint checks alignment, not provenance.

clauses.text: (never automate posting|ToS\s§?\s3\.1|decline and explain)
clauses.rationale: LinkedIn ToS §3.1 exposure: this is the only instruction telling the agent to decline scheduled/looped/unattended posting.
